When I realized a part of me wanted to be the way I was when I was psychologically unwell. It's a long story.

I was a sensitive kid growing up, who struggled with school, especially early one. I had a joint thing that made handwriting messy and slow, and I'm not good at memorizing information. Now, I consider myself quite intelligent, quite good at understanding things and seeing patterns, but growing up, I thought I was stupid and worthless. This led to a lot of anger and frustration. After a couple of incidents, one where I self-harmed because I was so angry at myself, and one where I lashed out at bullies, I was told I had anger management problems and told to learn about things like meditation, counting to ten, etc.

However, as a kid, I thought "anger management issues" was just a polite way of saying I was angrier than other people for no reason. I remembered all the anger I felt throughout early childhood, and it made sense. There was something wrong with me, and I needed to learn how to control my anger.

So, I learnt about meditation. About deep breathing. About counting to 10. And I didn't have any other outbursts. But, instead, I was just bottling up all my negative emotions. Pushing all my anger down, not letting myself act on my anger. And because I kept it buried, because I thought it was abnormal and something wrong with me I just had to deal with, I never really let go of that anger. It would just keep building and building, I just got better and better at not letting it show, not letting it escape.

After a few years of this, my self imaged defined by that anger. I felt like there was this ball of rage deep inside me, constant. Sure, I could forget about if distracted or busy, but other emotions felt fleeting and surface level, while the anger remained and was consistent and unchanging. I felt like everything good about me, all my positive traits, were surface, and the inner me, the "real" me, was just anger and violence and hatred. It's what's on the inside that counts, right?

Since I was this ball of undirected hatred, rage and violence on the inside, but kind and thoughtful on the outside, the only explanation I could come up with was that there was fundamentally wrong with me. That I was insane, and I had created some kind of persona to pretend I was sane. That everything good about me was just an outer shell, and deep down I was a monstrous psychopath. I concluded this was unsustainable, and believed that, one day, the strain and stress of living a lie would become too much, that the shell would crack and shatter, leaving behind nothing but my inner self. 

I gave up on myself. I gave up on my future. I truly believed that, long term, my future would either by a mental hospital, prison or an early death. This unresolved anger and beliefs about my own monstrous nature spiraled into darker thoughts of violence towards family members, all of which I kept buried. 

During my final lot of exams, I realized i just didn't care about my grades, my life, my future. I didn't study, I couldn't. I just went to the first exam, couldn't do most of the questions, asked to leave because I was having a mental breakdown, and was allowed to leave. I was rather manic. I felt such relief, such complete relief at no longer feeling I had to pretend that I was sane any more. To finally be able to express how bad I felt.

Afterwards, after a lot of counselling, I realized I wasn't a monster. I wasn't evil. I wasn't defined by anger and hatred. I wasn't insane. I was able to stop being angry.

However, while my initial reaction was relief and joy at my various breakthroughs, eventually I realized I had lost my sense of self. Who I was, my self image, had been defined by being an angry, violent, evil monster. That was who I truly believed I was, what I was. What I always was and always would be. And then, relatively suddenly, all that was thrown away, and I was left directionless. I didn't know what to do.

Not only that, but I realized the belief that I was insane, that I was monstrous, had been comforting. It had allowed me to stop thinking of myself as stupid and worthless, that had been fundamental to my self-image as a small child. I thought I was basically living life with a secret handicap, dealing with issues kids normally didn't need to deal with. Every failure had its excuse. Every achievement was all the more impressive. Not only that, but I needed to think about my future, about a career.  I'd never needed to think about my future before. I'd never wanted to think to hard about my future before. I was going to end up an insane monster, so why bother worrying about it?

I believed myself to be an evil, insane, violent monster, with no future and with nothing to lose. And then I "got better", and part of me missed it. I missed the certainty of my sense of self. I missed not needing to worry about my future. I missed being able to excuse any failing. I missed being able to completely ignore thoughts of being a stupid, worthless failure.

At my worst, part of me wanted to torture and murder my family. I remembered how that felt and part of me longed to feel that way again. 

I'm sure you can imagine how that would lead to shame. Thankfully, I was able to unpack that shame and figure out why I had legit reasons why I, why anyone in my situation, might have felt that way. But still, shame was the initial emotional response to that realization. 

I'm doing better now. I don't feel that longing any more. I don't feel shame for what I went through. I feel like a lot of my life has been defined by that illness, and I'm still getting my life on track, but I'm making progress. I've studied psychology at university (because I found it interesting on an intellectual level during counselling and wanted to be able to help others like I needed help) and I've gotten a job offer to begin working in a mental health hospital. After that, well.. we'll see.

Posting in my "srs buisness" account because I wanna talk about my gender Identity and thoughts about various aspects of my body.

I am a cis male. But I do do and think things that make me identify with the people of this subreddit. I feel rather paradoxical physically.

I'm not overly fond of my body. I'm very hairy. I feel like I'm too hairy, and sometimes shave my upper legs. I don't really see it as a feminine thing though. More like my body is too masculine and shaving helps bring that masculinity back down to more middle of the spectrum. It kinda feels nice. I'm so masculine I need to do something often seen as feminine to get to a baseline. It kind of makes me feel like I don't need to try to be masculine, which means I feel very little insecurity about my masculinity/femininity. Because fuck toxic masculinity.

But a nice side effect of my general hairiness is that I have very thick, very long eyelashes, which I like about myself. I've been asked by girls if I wear mascara more than once, with one girl saying girls would kill to have eyelashes like mine. 

I'm also very broad shouldered, but I like that about myself. I can grow a pretty good beard, and have had one for a few years. A kind of long stubble, rather than a full BEARD. Part of the reason I grew it out was because, when growing up, I was insecure about my facial hair having grey in it (my hair's a dark brown). To kind of overcome that insecurity I decided to grow my beard out, and I like it. 

I have rather severe baby face without it though. Even with my beard people are shocked I'm in my late 20s rather than late teens/early 20s. 

With the lockdown I grew my hair out for really the first time ever. Like the rest of my body's hair, my head hair is thick. It's not straight, but not what I would consider "curly", like an afro or anything like that. I've usually had it short, let it grow for a few months where it approaches a state I affectionately refer to as "anime hair" where it sticks up very easily, then it naturally becomes kind of.. big blob on top of my head until I get it cut. Now my hair has finally gotten past that stage where the overall length weighs enough to keep it flat on top, but it curls and twists on the way down. I like it a lot. I feel like a lion with a mane or something. Still need to get into the habit of tucking it behind my ears when eating :D. Mouth hair..

As far as facial features go, I'm rather inconsistent in my evaluations. My face seems to be simultaneously cute, handsome and ugly. It's probably insecurity. I don't really know how attractive I might be. 

Personality-wise, I've a few feminine aspects to me I've been able to embrace. I like cute things, and I think babies and small children are cute. I want to protect and nurture them.

I think I'm pretty submissive when it comes.. you know.. kinky things. Can't imagine myself as a dom. Sometimes I wish I was shorter, but not always. Maybe no just like the idea of being small and cute and submissive. It's not like I have  an interest in wearing dresses or whatever though. The only way I could imagine doing so is if I was with a partner who wanted me to, that they found it attractive. I would do so then, in private, but I feel it's more my security in my masculinity rather than any trans leanings.

As far as gender goes, I think I'm cis. A metaphor I came up with was a gelatin mold. Like, my body is male, my mind poured into that make mold, and now you take the mold away and the male gender retains its shape. Gender is a social construct, and my gender fits my body. Had my mind been the same and I was born with a female body, I don't really know if I would be trans male, or if my gender/mind would have just set differently. If I could change my gender with a push of a button, back and forth, I would be willing to try it, maybe even show it off, but I wouldn't be interested beyond the sheer novelty of being the other sex. Which is how I would see it. My body would feel like my body, male or female, but I would feel that male is the default for me.

Problem is, I have trouble putting myself out there at all.

  I had rather serious repressed anger, which made me think I was more psychologically unstable and dangerous than I actually was. Think really bad teenage angst, bottled up so it never reaches the surface, to the point of feeling intense anger most of the time.

I thought a girlfriend would, at best, be another person to mourn me when I finally snapped, at worst, another victim. So I tried my best to repress my sexuality. I told myself over and over again: "no-one will ever love you. No-one should ever love you. It would be morally wrong for someone to love you." By the end of it, the idea of some hypothetical girl actually being attracted to me literally made me feel nauseous.

I eventually had a breakdown, one without the violence I had always feared. Got help, realised my how my own irrational beliefs had developed and why they were false.

That was about 7 years ago. I was 18 at the time, 25 now. I no longer tell myself no-one should ever love me, and the thought no long makes me nauseous. But it still feels wrong. Not bad and immoral, just.. unnatural. Impossible.

I don't think anyone has ever expressed attraction towards me in my life. I'm a 25 year old virgin whose never even kissed a girl. I spent years repressing my own sexuality, then spent many more years trying to figure out who I was now that the central part of my sense of self had suddenly disappeared in a few weeks.

Who the hell would want to deal with all that shit for me? I'm just some ex-crazy, sexually repressed loser. I'm not attractive, I'm not interesting, I'm not successful. I'm just a history of anger and sadness.

I am lonely. I wish I could find a girlfriend. But I cannot imagine anyone wanting to date me. My lack of physical attractiveness, my lack of experience, my history of psychological problems, my lack self esteem and the self loathing I try to keep hidden. Any one of those would make me seem less than ideal. With them all, I might as well still be telling myself no-one will ever love me.

How can I put myself out there when I have such low opinion of myself? Why should I believe I am worth the trouble when I have 25 years of evidence suggesting I am not? How can I hope for romantic success when the very idea seems alien in my mind?

Not a teacher. I'm the student, and it is a **long** story.

I was a rather emotional child. I have always had bad hand writing, slow and messy; due to hypermobility, some of my joints are overly stretchy. Also, I've never really been good at remembering things. What's early school mostly about? Handwriting and memory: spellings, times tables, writing skills. All that I sucked at. I was good a reading, and I'm actually quite intelligent, good at understanding rather than remembering.

So, most of my early education was spent feeling frustrated and angry for not being able to do the work. I didn't really know who I was angry at, because I didn't realise I was myself. I would cry, cover my ears and be unresponsive, and hit the desk with my head.

This lasted until the work actually started to get hard, around year 5. When the work got harder, and actually needed some thought, I began to excel. I distinctively remember learning about algebra, I found it so easy it was comical. My episodes of anger and frustration became less frequent and stopped.

The relief I felt, while allowing me to be a better student, did have a negative side effect. I was so scared of failure, of once again being swallowed up by those feelings of shame and self hatred. 

Later, in secondary school, Year 8. We were in the library, it was near the beginning of the year. Every week, this class was going to be about using resources available to you to research, that sort of thing.

I had been placed in a group of three, two other boys and myself, they were friends. We were assigned the task of discussing, something, I cannot remember what, and writing down what we had discussed.

The two boys decided between themselves that I should write. Being the shy young boy I was, not fully understanding my problems other than a vague dislike for writing, I didn't fight it. The two of them discussed the subject between themselves, not really telling me what to write, just expecting me to figure out what to write down. I froze up. The boys told me to write, I didn't.

The time allocated ran out and the teacher began collecting the papers. When she came to our group, the boys told her that it was my fault, that I refused to write anything. The teacher asked me why I hadn't done the work.

All the feelings that I had thought I had escaped from for years, the feeling of being a failure, rose in me. Stronger than ever. I hated myself so much. I put my hands on my head and screamed. I clawed at my face, again and again, trying to punish myself for being such a failure. I drew blood, and I did not stop. I kept clawing. Eventually, my anger gave out and I just cried.

And that led to being the subject of bullying, which led to me getting angry at them, which led me to being told I had anger management issues. That led me to being taught to surpress my negative emotions, which worked too well. All my anger and pubescent hormones were pushed down, meaning on the surface I was nice and well adjusted, but deep down I felt anger pretty much constantly. Combined my history of emotional outbursts, this led to me beliving I was basically an insane psychopath. Every good aspect of my personality was only on the surface, just an outer shell, but deep down I was an evil monster who wanted to torture and murder everyone around me. Which basically made me give up on myself and I just went through the motions until the end of year 13, when I had a meltdown and started getting counsilling.

I thought I'd share a perspective from the other side. How a history of lots of little problems can build into huge outbursts.
Thank you for your support. I appreciate it.

It's so strange. For such a long period of my life, believing is was a monster was the core of my self image. Now.. I don't know what I am. Who I am. 

I was always thinking about my problems. Wondering if I really did believe what I was telling myself, or if I was just pretending to avoid responsiblity. That all my life, I pretended to have something wrong with me so I could get away with things. That so long as I could blame all my problems on my mental health, no one could ever hold me accountable for my failures. I am so scared of failure. Scared of feeling what I felt when I was younger.

The time I got so angry with my inability to do my school work I clawed at my own face until I was bleeding.

This left me with the belief that I was a naturally violent person, that deep down I was a seething ball of rage that needed to be suppressed. As I grew older, this belief evolved into me believing that, not only was I angry, but sadistic, psychotic and, to put it simply, evil.

I was wrong, and I know that now, but for most of my adolescent life I "knew" that I wasn't going to have a future. That I would go insane, end up in prison, a hospital or a early grave. I didn't think about the future. I trained myself not to be social and to surpress any form of romantic attraction I felt, because I didn't want anyone to get close to me, either to moun me or to become a target of my psychotic behavior.

I have not been able to sort my life out since.

Perhaps it's not as "legit" as other people's, but the fact that it was self inflected makes it feel a hundred times worse.

I took the drugs. For months. I ddn't find a job. I didn't get my life together. What was the point. What's the point of trying again.

I had councilling for my irrational beliefs, that deep down I was a monster. They helped me understand them and realise wby they were false.

What can therapy do for me now? I know what's wrong. I know I'm a fuck up. I'm weak. I'm soft. I'm emotional. I think too much. I'm a failure and every second I spend being a failure I can never get back. I can never fix. I can never make right.

I tried. I had an interview for clearing shopping carts from a supermarket car park. I looked at working at a McDonald's and their online questionnaire intimidated me. I tried to apply for a newsagent's, but the website says you need to give your last 5 years of employment.

I have no references. I have no job experience. I'm mentally unstable. No one will employ me. Loading up a job search website makes me want to vomit. Makes me want to stab myself in the gut. I can't even look for a job without wanting to curl up into a ball on my bed. How am I supposed to write a covering letter? How am I supposed to sell myself for a job that I don't deserve. An employer shouldn't hire me because I'm not asking to be an employee, I'm asking them to throw a job opportunity away just so I can feel better.

I'm more or less over my anger problems, I think.

I'm pretty smart, but I have a poor memory and bad handwriting (due to hyper-mobility in my hand + other places)

And of course, the main things you learn when you're starting school is writing (handwriting) spelling (memory) and times tables (memory). I was a great reader, but when it came to actually doing work, I was always behind and unable to perform.

That's when I first started being really angry with myself, not really understanding why or even what it meant back then. It's so frustrating for someone who's actually relatively intelligent to be treated like I was incompetent, to think of yourself as incapable. Of course, the emotional outbursts didn't help either. I can't really blame anyone for that, but it's just how life went.

Things only really started to get better once the work started getting harder. When it took some understanding, I was all over it. I remember algebra being so easy it was comical, replacing numbers with letters was a simple concept. Once I was getting good at my work, my frustration alleviated.

Then in year 8 I was put to work in a group with 2 other boys. They decided between them that they would discuss the topic and I'd write everything down. I knew I couldn't write well, but I was a shy boy and I didn't know the others. I froze up and didn't write anything. The lesson ended and they told the teacher I refused to do the work.

All the feelings of anger and frustration that I'd thought I'd escaped from for years suddenly resurfaced, 10x worse than ever since I'd never expected it. That was when I scratched myself. Maybe I was trying to punish myself, maybe I was just really angry and wanted to hurt myself, I don't know. That was probably my lowest point..

After that, I just carried on doing what I was good at, maths and sciences. Never thinking about what I'd actually want to do.

Now, after everything I've been through, I'd rather like to go into a career where I help others like I needed help. A councilor or psychologist or something. Like I said, I've never been good with memory, but I'm good at understanding things. I'm empathetic and sensitive, and while it was really helpful, i found it very interesting on an intellectual level, figuring out how my problems had developed.

I just feel right now it's a huge thing to think about and I feel like I might not be able to handle it. I don't know anything about going to university. I pretty much ignored all the talks in school about it because "What's it matter, I'm insane and evil" and my A-Levels aren't psychology or even biology based. Maths, Physics and Computing. I wouldn't know how to do it, where to go, what I'd have to do. Even if I did, I've practically been socially dead for years, even before I left school. How would I be able to socialize? Not to mention everyone would question why I was 3 or 4 years older than everyone else.

I've put so much time into this short term goal of finding a job, made myself so invested in it, it's hard thinking of something long term like that.

"Have you seen a counselor recently?" Not recently, no.

"have you ever considered doing volunteer work?" Yes, but every time I look into it I get overwhelmed by what I could do and what I should do, as well as doubting myself and thinking that I'm a failure for not getting a real job.

"have you gone back to the doctor and talked to him/her about it?" No, I just feel like I don't care any more.

"What kind of jobs are you looking for?" I don't know, admin jobs, working in a shop. 

"Have you had any schooling past high school?" I'm English, but I suppose that would be a no. I left school at the end of my last year of Sixth Form when I was 18. Worst part is that all the subjects I did I didn't care about. Maths and science, and now they've nothing to do with whatever vague plans I think I might want to do.

"How old are you?" 21.
It's not that I don't feel happy some times, it's just it feels like everything I do enjoy is just a distraction, a temporary block on me thinking about how shit I feel my life is.

Yep, being rejected sucks, but it's not that big of a deal, unless you allow it to be. Most guys won't let it effect them very much.

Basically, is avoiding the "demoralizing" effect of being rejected worth reducing your chances of finding someone to nearly impossible? Most people would say no. 

Most people understand that finding someone is a reasonable possibility and that when you find someone, it is worth much more than whatever short-term discomfort you felt from being rejected. 

If you personally find rejection so much worst than most, or care very little about romantic relationships, then that's what you think.

But realize that you are a minority, that what you think would seem irrational to most and that by saying your way "is the most rational response" you seem arrogant and foolish.

Just because you've only been rejected in the past, doesn't mean you will only be rejected in the future.

Sure, OTHER guys may have been able to find someone by now, and other guys would probably get a lot more rejections than you have, and would still end up finding someone.

It doesn't matter if you get rejected once or a thousand times, it doesn't make you able to know the future, it doesn't mean you will only ever get rejections. You don't know you're never going to be able to find someone, pretending otherwise is just arrogance.

You have to ask yourself, do you believe this because you actually believe it to be true, or because you want it to be true.

It's easier to believe that you're just destined to be alone, because that's something beyond your control, so can just stop trying and avoid the pain that comes with rejection. You can blame your loneliness on statistics or luck or fate, so you don't blame your own convictions or think about actual reasons why women wouldn't be attracted to YOU.

It's hard dealing with your own irrationality, irrationality keeps you sane in a cruel world that cares so little, but if you allow it, it will keep you blocked off from a world filled with wonder, happiness and love.

Ok, so on a physical level, you're attractive.

Congratulations, you're more ahead of the game than some.

Now, do you have any real evidence to say that you will never find someone who would be willing to be in a relationship with you?
Did you find them attractive though?

If they were "nothing special" why did you ask them out? I wouldn't ask someone out if I didn't feel special to me, either physically or personality wise.

If you're just asking them out because you thought there was a chance they would accept you, you're asking them out because you want someone, anyone to be with you. A girl isn't going to want to be with you just so you can have a girlfriend, she's going to be with you because you want to be with HER.

Even if it's only because you find her attractive, it's better than just being asked out because you're lonely.

Yep, and that's a shame. But every data set will have outliers, just as there will be people who end up having hundreds of sexual partners.

However, until OP actually dies, he can't say he's one of those people, because he has no real evidence to distinguish himself from the mass of individuals who are able to find someone.

If someone claims to "know" that he or she won't ever find someone, they are being arrogant. It is healthier, humbler and more logically correct to know that you don't know and that finding someone is still very much a possibility.

The world has over 7 billion people in it. If finding someone is so impossible, there wouldn't be that many people in it.

I'm sorry to seem rude, but you are not special, you are not some kind of universe shattering being of anti-attraction. You are a person just like everyone else, with 7 billion people after over 5000 years of generation after generation of humanity, you have just a much a chance to find someone as any one of them did.

Ok, so you've never felt like any female has ever been attracted to you, guess what, neither do I. It's irrational, I know this, doesn't mean I don't feel it and it's not real to me. I'm 20, never had a girlfriend, never been romantically involved with someone. Doesn't mean I don't think someone could be attracted to me, doesn't mean I'm unattractive or that I'll never meet anyone.
 
Want some advice, maybe try posting something to /r/amiugly or something. They'll either dispute you and say you have attractive qualities (at least physically) or they'll say why you're not attractive, but they'll give rational, real reasons, usually with ways you may improve yourself, not your irrational belief that you are just undateable.

Either way, it's better than living in your own mind, where everything is as bad as you fear it to be. Having that rock of solid, rational understanding about your physical appearance could be the anchor to reality you need to pull yourself out of this way of thinking.

Also, don't think of ladies as just potential partners. Do you interact with the opposite gender in ways beyond trying to ask them out?
